cards.explanation: The answer is that they stumble and perish. Psalm 9:3 says, "When my enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before You." Retreating doesn't get them out of it, friends. The verse puts the retreat and the stumbling together. This is a heavy line.

The answer is a judge on His throne judging righteously. Psalm 9:4 says, "You sit on Your throne judging righteously." A judge sits, listens and decides what's right, and here the LORD has upheld David's just cause. That's a steady picture, friends. Nobody has to wonder who's in charge of the room.
The answer is True. Psalm 9:5 says, "You have erased their name forever and ever." Forever and ever, friends. That's not pencil, and it's not even pencil with a cheap eraser.

The answer is False. The enemy is gone, but David doesn't say the LORD fades away. Psalm 9:7 says, "But the LORD abides forever…" He also "…has established His throne for judgment." No fading, friends, and no expiration date.

The answer is a refuge and a stronghold. Psalm 9:9 says, "The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble." Both of those are places you can run INTO. In times of trouble, that's what David says the LORD is, friends.

The answer is True. Psalm 9:10 says, "…for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You." The verse also says that those who know His name trust in Him. Seek Him, friends, and you're not talking to an empty room.
The answer is "ignore." Psalm 9:12 says, "He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted." When the afflicted cry out, He doesn't look past them. Not once, friends.

The answer is that David wants to declare God's praises and rejoice. Psalm 9:14 gives his purpose: "…that I may declare all Your praises…" He also wants to "…rejoice in Your salvation." Praise and rejoicing are what he's asking to be lifted up for, friends.

The answer is the nations themselves. Psalm 9:15 says, "The nations have fallen into a pit of their making; their feet are caught in the net they have hidden." They dug it and they hid it, then they landed in it. That's the oldest trap in the book, friends, and it's on the people who set it.

The answer is False. The nations who forget God are headed for Sheol (Psalm 9:17), but David doesn't say the needy will always be forgotten. Psalm 9:18 says, "For the needy will not always be forgotten; nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed."
The answer is that they are only men. Psalm 9:20 says, "let the nations know they are but men." It's a humbling reminder, friends. That's the whole ask in this line.
The answer is the needy. Psalm 10:2 says, "In pride the wicked pursue the needy…" They do it in pride. The needy are the ones being pursued, friends.
The answer is none at all. Psalm 10:4 says, "in all his schemes there is no God." Not one scheme with God in it, friends. Pride filled up the whole space.

The answer is False. The first half is true, friends, since the wicked man leaves God out of his schemes. But Psalm 10:5 says, "Your lofty judgments are far from him…" They're far from him, not close.

The answer is a lion in a thicket. Psalm 10:9 says, "He lies in wait like a lion in a thicket; he lurks to seize the oppressed…" A lion sits still in the brush and waits to pounce, friends. That's the picture.

The answer is that God has forgotten and never sees. Psalm 10:11 says, "He says to himself, “God has forgotten; He hides His face and never sees.”" That's what the wicked man tells himself, friends. It's his claim about God, and I'm glad the psalm doesn't leave it standing alone.

The answer is False. The wicked man is not sure God will make him answer. Psalm 10:13 has him saying to himself, "You will never call me to account." He's sure no reckoning is coming, friends, and that's what the psalmist is arguing against.

The answer is "fatherless." Psalm 10:14 says, "The victim entrusts himself to You; You are the helper of the fatherless." The LORD is the helper of the fatherless, friends. That's a good thing to have in your corner.

The answer is the arm of the wicked. Psalm 10:15 says, "Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer; call him to account for his wickedness until none is left to be found." That's the psalmist's request to God, friends. What he asks God to break is the arm.

The answer is "humble." Psalm 10:17 says, "You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble; You will strengthen their hearts." The humble get heard and strengthened. That's a good deal for anybody, friends.

The answer is True. Psalm 10:17 says, "You will incline Your ear…" and verse 18 goes on, "…to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more." It's a good place for the psalm to land, friends, with God leaning in to listen.
